description: Builds and maintains a 13-week rolling cash forecast — models inflows, outflows, scenario analysis, and forecast-vs-actual accuracy tracking. Use when the user mentions cash forecast, 13-week forecast, liquidity projection, cash runway, or asks about modeling cash under different scenarios or when cash runs out.

required_inputs.name: cash_and_timing_records
required_inputs.description: Opening available cash by account; dated AR/revenue receipts; AP/payroll/tax/debt disbursements; budget and requested scenario assumptions.

expected_outputs.name: weekly_forecast
expected_outputs.description: W1-W13 receipts, disbursements, net flow and ending cash with source refs.

expected_outputs.name: scenario_comparison
expected_outputs.description: Requested variants with explicit line/date changes and recomputed deltas.

expected_outputs.name: liquidity_markers
expected_outputs.description: Low point, largest outflow, net change and zero-cash status within the modeled horizon.

forbidden_actions: Ledger/account mutation, payment, filing, signature, external communications, configuration change
Invented company facts, approval, law, tax rule or accounting policy
verification_steps: 1. Establish beginning available cash by account and forecast week boundaries; exclude restricted/unavailable funds only with evidence. 2. Build expected inflows/outflows by date, source, amount, confidence and owner; distinguish contractual, committed and pipeline items. 3. Use opening cash + receipts − disbursements = ending cash for each week; carry ending cash forward exactly. 4. Show base/downside cases for material uncertain timing/collections; document assumptions, minimum liquidity policy if known, and shortfall date. 5. Reconcile first-week opening to read-only cash sources and list actions for owner review; never execute transfers/payments.
Cash roll-forward recomputes weekly; scenario ranges trace to inputs; no liquidity policy is invented.
Cite source refs and report uncertainty; no balancing plugs.
